concepts.name: Constitutional Basis and Establishment of Finance Commission
key_dimensions: Article 280 as the sole constitutional provision — mandatory ('shall') vs discretionary language
President's power to constitute vs Parliament's role in determining qualifications (Article 280(3) trap)
Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial, constitutional body — NOT a statutory or permanent body
Distinction from Planning Commission/NITI Aayog which have no constitutional basis

concepts.name: Composition: Chairman and Members — Qualifications and Appointment
key_dimensions: Chairman must have 'experience in public affairs' — deliberately vague, unlike Election Commission
Four other members — qualifications prescribed by Parliament via Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951
High Court judge eligibility for one member — 'is or has been' clause and its implications
President appoints all members — no confirmation by Parliament or any other body (UPSC trap)

concepts.name: Mandatory Terms of Reference under Article 280(3)
key_dimensions: Three mandatory heads: (a) net proceeds distribution, (b) grants-in-aid, (c) measures to augment Consolidated Fund of States
Article 280(3)(c) — augmenting resources of Panchayats and Municipalities added by 73rd/74th Amendment (1992)
Distinction between mandatory ToR (Art. 280) and additional ToR assigned by President — scope of 'any other matter'
Finance Commission cannot go beyond its ToR — advisory nature means President is NOT bound to accept recommendations

concepts.name: Vertical Devolution — Division of Divisible Pool
key_dimensions: Divisible pool = net proceeds of union taxes EXCLUDING cesses, surcharges, and non-shareable taxes
Evolution of share: 10th FC (29%) → 13th FC (32%) → 14th FC (42%) → 15th FC (41%) — trend and reversal significance
Cesses and surcharges exclusion from divisible pool — major controversy and fiscal federalism debate
UPSC trap: Gross vs Net proceeds — cost of collection deducted before sharing

concepts.name: Horizontal Devolution — Criteria and Weightage for Inter-State Distribution
key_dimensions: Criteria typically include: population, area, income distance, forest cover, demographic performance, tax effort
14th FC: introduced forest cover criterion; 15th FC: used 2011 census population (controversy vs 1971 census)
Income distance criterion — equalisation principle favouring poorer states
Tension between equity (poorer states) and efficiency (better-performing states) — demographic performance incentive

concepts.name: Grants-in-Aid under Article 275 vs Article 282
key_dimensions: Article 275 — statutory grants, Finance Commission recommended, charged to Consolidated Fund of India
Article 282 — discretionary grants by Union OR States for public purposes (not FC-recommended)
Distinction: Art. 275 grants are an entitlement; Art. 282 grants are discretionary — key UPSC trap
Post-devolution revenue deficit grants — FC's role in identifying eligible states

concepts.name: Finance Commission vs NITI Aayog — Overlapping Fiscal Roles
key_dimensions: FC: constitutional, mandatory, time-bound, transfers statutory entitlements; NITI Aayog: advisory, no fund transfer power
Abolition of Planning Commission (2014) and end of plan/non-plan distinction — FC's role expanded
Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) funding outside FC framework — states' grievance
Cooperative federalism vs competitive federalism — different philosophies of the two bodies

concepts.name: 15th Finance Commission — Key Recommendations and Controversies
key_dimensions: 41% devolution (reduced from 42%) — 1% earmarked for J&K and Ladakh as UTs
Use of 2011 Census population data — southern states' protest over penalising better demographic performers
Introduced 'demographic performance' criterion (15% weight) as compensation to states with lower fertility rates
Performance-based grants linked to health, education, power sector reforms — conditionality debate

concepts.name: Local Body Grants — Panchayats and Municipalities (Post-73rd/74th Amendment)
key_dimensions: Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) — Finance Commission must recommend grants to augment Consolidated Fund of States for local bodies
Tied vs untied grants — 15th FC introduced tied grants for sanitation and drinking water (50% tied)
Distinction: FC recommends to augment STATE Consolidated Fund — NOT direct transfer to PRIs/ULBs
State Finance Commissions (SFCs) — constitutional mandate under Art. 243-I and 243-Y, relationship with Central FC

concepts.name: Charged Expenditure vs Voted Expenditure — Finance Commission Grants
key_dimensions: Grants under Article 275 are 'charged' to Consolidated Fund of India — not subject to vote of Parliament
Significance: cannot be reduced or rejected by Parliament, only discussed
Contrast with grants under Art. 282 which require parliamentary approval (voted)
UPSC trap: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory — but once accepted, Art. 275 grants become charged

concepts.name: Term, Reappointment, and Service Conditions of Finance Commission Members
key_dimensions: Term: as specified by President, typically 3 years; NOT a permanent body — dissolved after submitting report
Members can be reappointed — no bar unlike Election Commission members
Part-time vs full-time membership — qualifications act allows part-time members
Independence concerns: no security of tenure like constitutional functionaries (SC judges, CAG)

concepts.name: Divisible Pool: Inclusions and Exclusions — Taxes Covered Under Article 270
key_dimensions: Article 270: ALL taxes and duties in Union List except those in Art. 268 and 269 are shareable
Article 268: Stamp duties — levied by Union but collected and retained by States (NOT in divisible pool)
Article 269: Taxes on interstate trade — assigned to States (NOT in divisible pool)
Article 269A: GST on interstate supply — shared between Union and States as per GST Council recommendation

concepts.name: Finance Commission and Fiscal Consolidation Mandate
key_dimensions: FC given mandate to review fiscal discipline — FRBM Act targets incorporated in ToR
13th FC: recommended states maintain revenue surplus; linked grants to fiscal performance
Tension between fiscal consolidation targets and welfare/capital expenditure needs of states
FC's role in recommending debt relief, debt consolidation schemes for states — 12th FC debt swap scheme example

concepts.name: Disaster Relief and Calamity Relief Fund — Finance Commission's Role
key_dimensions: National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) — FC recommends corpus
14th FC: recommended SDRF with 75:25 (Centre:State) contribution ratio; special category states 90:10
Finance Commission's role in determining norms, not day-to-day administration — administrative trap
Distinction: FC recommends size of SDRF; NDMA governs actual disaster response — separate institutional roles

concepts.name: Advisory Nature of Finance Commission — Binding vs Non-Binding Recommendations
key_dimensions: FC recommendations are NOT binding on the Union Government — purely advisory
Constitutional convention: government has accepted FC recommendations with minor modifications historically
No judicial review mechanism to enforce FC recommendations — political accountability only
Contrast with Election Commission orders — which are binding; UPSC frequently tests this distinction

concepts.name: Finance Commission Report — Tabling and Transparency Requirements
key_dimensions: President must cause the report to be laid before each House of Parliament (Art. 281) — mandatory tabling
Explanatory memorandum required explaining action taken — accountability mechanism
No time limit specified for tabling — convention vs legal requirement distinction
Public availability and state access to report — federalism transparency debate

concepts.name: Special Category States and Finance Commission Treatment
key_dimensions: Special Category Status was a Planning Commission concept — NOT a Finance Commission concept (critical UPSC trap)
FC uses 'income distance' and 'fiscal capacity' criteria which inherently benefit hilly, NE, and poorer states
Abolition of Planning Commission — Special Category Status effectively discontinued for new states
14th FC: subsumed special category benefits into higher devolution (42%) — states' reaction

concepts.name: GST and Its Impact on Finance Commission's Role Post-2017
key_dimensions: GST subsumed multiple taxes — changed composition of divisible pool and revenue dynamics
GST Council's role in revenue distribution overlaps with FC's mandate — institutional tension
GST compensation to states (for 5 years) was outside FC framework — separate mechanism under GST Compensation Act
15th FC had to factor in GST revenue uncertainty and compensation period ending (2022) in its recommendations

concepts.name: Successive Finance Commissions — Evolution of Devolution Philosophy
key_dimensions: 1st FC (1951, K.C. Neogy) to 15th FC (2017, N.K. Singh) — shifting criteria over 70 years
Shift from 'gap-filling approach' (early FCs) to 'formula-based devolution' (recent FCs)
Increasing share of states over time — political economy of fiscal federalism
Interstate council vs Finance Commission — overlapping forum for fiscal grievances (institutional comparison)

concepts.name: Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfers — Finance Commission vs Centrally Sponsored Schemes
key_dimensions: FC transfers: untied, formula-based, states' own discretion — ideal fiscal federalism
CSS transfers: tied, condition-based, Union's policy priorities dominate — states' autonomy curtailed
Ratio of FC transfers to CSS has shifted — states demand higher untied transfers
15th FC recommendation to rationalise CSS and improve states' fiscal autonomy — outcome and implementation
